page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. At the top: running head centred, page number at top right. Below that, two round medallion portraits side by side, with their legends printed around them. Under them, one column of text in two paragraphs, starting with capitalised lead-in words.

main_text.p: PHILIBERTVS Sabaudiæ Dux octauus, succedit patri Philippo anno mundi 5457. à Christo nato 1495. Hic pietatem summopere coluit, magnanimus, speciosissimus, atque omnibus acceptissimus fuit, pulcher etiam ob elegantiâ cognominatus. Margaretâ coniugem accepit, quam ex Maria Caroli Burgūdię Ducis filia susceperat Maximilianus, obiit multa commendatione dignus, nullis interim relictis liberis: quare ei Carolus frater successit. Vide Allobrogum, siue Sabaudiæ Chro.*

MARGARETA Imperatoris Maximiliani filia, ut dictum est, ac Philiberti supradicti relicta, animum pudicũ atque amorem erga virum castissimum testata est, tum quòd nullum superinduxerit coniugem, vitâ perpetuò cælibem ac laudatissimam ducés:tum quòd in urbe quam vulgo Burgum in Bressia vocât, templũ nobile ac celebratissimum extruxerit, quod inter Europæ nuper structa ædificia, tanquâ opus rarum ac percelebre prædicatur: nec id quidem ob templi amplitudinem, sed potius ob artis ornamenta ac splendorem, ut omnium conspicientium oculos in admirationem trahat. Verùm ædificij decus ac splendorem longè superat sepulchrũ candidissimo marmore extructum: ubi extat amantissimi coniugis effigies ad vivum expressa: in quod signum quicquid ars sculpendi unquam valuit, contulisse, ac deprompsisse videtur: hæc Ducis effigies hinc & inde habet duarum Margaretarum marmorea simulachra ad vivum etiam formata: nempe Margaretæ uxoris prædictæ, & Margaretæ alterius, quæ Ducis mater extitit. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Two round medallion portraits (engravings) at the top: left, a man in a flat cap, legend "D. SAB." and "PHILIBERTVS"; right, a veiled woman with a flower, legend "MARGARETA" and "MAX. FIL.". The legends are transcribed above as printed lines. The "*" after "Chro." and the ornament after "celebratissimum" are printed signs, copied as seen; the ornament is not reproduced exactly. Some letters in "ducés:tum" and "Burgūdię" are small and may be misread. "Vide ut supra" is printed in the last line.
